text: Congratulations to Ruben Culqui Salazar, who passed his PhD viva on the distribution and ecology of caecilians in Ecuador. Well done Dr Culqui Salazar!
Congratulations to Hafiza Maira Munir on passing her PhD viva, for her work on lesser wax moths. Well done Dr Munir!

Delighted to say we have been awarded a [Wild Animal Initiative Challenge Grant](https://www.wildanimalinitiative.org/blog/2026-grants) to develop, test and validate indicators of wild insect welfare. Using Dubia cockroaches, two-spotted crickets and carrion beetles, we'll measure stress responses, fat reserves and movement, check them against cognitive bias tests, and then take the most practical indicators out to wild carrion beetle populations.
Congratulations to Rebecca Chen on her PhD viva in May, on the genomics of sexually selected traits in black grouse, with Joe Hoffman and Kees van Oers.
Welcome to Karen Salazar Niño, who joins the group with a Marie Curie Fellowship to study collective sperm movement.

In October I was invited to the [Max Planck Institute of Animal Behaviour](https://www.ab.mpg.de) to talk about wild animal welfare. Many thanks to my hosts Inge Mueller, Wolfgang Fiedler and Daniel Zuniga; it was a great visit. At the end of the month I also visited Bielefeld University to present our HFSP work on sperm evolution. Great to catch up with Joe Hoffman, Rebecca Chen and Kees van Oers.

Busy summer so far. Blake Morton, Simon Clegg and I have been awarded a [Wild Animal Initiative grant](https://www.wildanimalinitiative.org/blog/large-grants-2024) to study parasites and pathogens in urban wildlife, with a new PhD starting in October. We've also had several papers published, including [fox genetics in Australia](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ece3.11212) and [sperm–egg coevolution](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspb.2024.0525).
Some personal news (which I never really like sharing): I was promoted to Professor of Animal Ecology.
